title: Duchy of Thuringia
capsule: The early Duchy of Thuringia emerged under Frankish overlordship after the Merovingian and Saxon destruction of the Thuringian kingdom around 531 CE, with King Dagobert I appointing Radulf as duke around 632. The duchy struggled against both Frankish centralization and peripheral pressures; after the last early ducal line's extinction around 719 it was absorbed into Carolingian administration. The title was eventually revived in a new form: from 1131 a Landgraviate of Thuringia under the Ludowingian dynasty — whose Landgrave Ludwig IV married Saint Elizabeth of Hungary — rose to major importance before the male line failed in 1247, passing the territory to the Wettin margraves of Meissen.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries of the early Frankish duchy are only approximately reconstructable from administrative documents; the eastern frontier with Slavic peoples is particularly uncertain.
